title: Garvey founds the UNIA
text: Marcus Garvey launches the Universal Negro Improvement Association in Kingston. Its red, black and green flag and its call to look to Africa shape everything that follows.

title: The Holy Piby
text: Robert Athlyi Rogers publishes his “Black man's Bible” in Newark, New Jersey. It names Garvey an apostle and will be read by early Rasta preachers.

title: The Royal Parchment Scroll
text: Fitz Balintine Pettersburg's mystical text of Black supremacy circulates in Jamaica. Howell later borrows from it.

title: A King is crowned
text: On 2 November, Ras Tafari Makonnen is crowned Haile Selassie I in Addis Ababa. Jamaican preachers read it as prophecy fulfilled.

title: Howell convicted
text: After preaching that Selassie, not King George V, was the true sovereign, Leonard Howell is convicted of sedition and jailed.

title: Italy invades Ethiopia
text: Mussolini's invasion in October rouses Black communities worldwide. Ethiopia becomes a cause, and Selassie a symbol of resistance.

title: Ethiopian World Federation
text: Dr Malaku Bayen founds the EWF in New York to rally support for Ethiopia. Its Jamaican branches become a Rasta meeting ground.

title: Pinnacle founded
text: Howell establishes a self-sufficient commune at Pinnacle in St Catherine, home to hundreds of followers.

title: First raid on Pinnacle
text: Police raid the commune and arrest Howell and others. Raids continue through the next decade.

title: Land at Shashamane
text: Haile Selassie grants 500 acres at Shashamane, south of Addis Ababa, for people of the African diaspora who supported Ethiopia.

title: The first dreadlocks
text: Young Rastas in Kingston, linked to the Youth Black Faith, begin wearing locks as a covenant and a rejection of Babylon's grooming.

title: Pinnacle destroyed
text: A raid largely destroys the commune, and police clear the last residents in 1958. Its people scatter into West Kingston, where the movement grows faster and louder.

title: Prince Emmanuel's convention
text: A mass gathering at Back-O-Wall in March. Charles Edwards emerges as Prince Emmanuel and founds the Bobo Shanti.

title: The ships that never came
text: Claudius Henry sells cards promising passage to Africa on 5 October. Hundreds sell their belongings and wait; no ships arrive.

title: The UCWI report
text: Scholars M. G. Smith, Roy Augier and Rex Nettleford study the movement and urge the government to treat Rastas with respect.

title: Mission to Africa
text: A government delegation, with Rastafari members, visits Ethiopia, Nigeria, Ghana and other states to explore repatriation.

title: Coral Gardens
text: Over Easter, after a deadly clash near Montego Bay, police round up Rastas across Jamaica. Many are beaten, jailed and forcibly shaved.

title: Selassie at the UN
text: On 4 October Selassie addresses the United Nations on racial equality. Bob Marley later sets the speech to music as “War”.

title: Grounation Day
text: On 21 April a huge crowd floods Palisadoes airport for Selassie's visit. He waits on the aircraft steps until elder Mortimo Planno calms the crowd.

title: Twelve Tribes founded
text: Vernon Carrington, known as Prophet Gad, founds the Twelve Tribes of Israel, the most open of the Mansions.

title: The Rodney riots
text: The Guyanese historian Walter Rodney, who had held “groundings” with Rastas, is barred from Jamaica. Kingston erupts.

title: The Ethiopian Church arrives
text: The Ethiopian Orthodox Church opens in Jamaica. Many Rastas are baptised; others reject it as a step away from Selassie's divinity.

title: Selassie's death
text: Deposed by the Derg in 1974, Selassie dies in custody in August 1975. Many Rastas reject the reports or hold that Jah cannot die.

title: Exodus
text: Reggae carries Rastafari across the world. Albums by Bob Marley, Burning Spear and Culture take Rasta theology into homes on every continent.

title: Berhane Selassie
text: Bob Marley is baptised into the Ethiopian Orthodox Church as Berhane Selassie, months before his death in 1981.

title: A Rasta in the Senate
text: Barbara Makeda Blake Hannah becomes an independent senator, the first Rastafarian in Jamaica's Parliament.

title: Dawkins case, UK
text: The Court of Appeal rules Rastafari are not an ethnic group under race law, in the case of a man refused a job unless he cut his locks.

title: Sacrament recognised
text: Jamaica amends its drug laws, decriminalising small amounts of ganja and permitting sacramental use by Rastafari.

title: An apology
text: Prime Minister Andrew Holness formally apologises for Coral Gardens, 54 years on, and a compensation trust is set up for survivors.

title: Recognised in Ethiopia
text: Ethiopia announces identity cards for long-stateless Rastafari residents, many of them living at Shashamane.

title: South Africa rules
text: The Constitutional Court allows private cannabis use, after a long legal fight led by the Rastafari lawyer Gareth Prince.

title: Locks at Achimota
text: Ghana's High Court orders Achimota School to admit two Rastafari students it had turned away over their locks.

title: Land returned
text: On Good Friday, 3 April, land titles in Albion, St James are handed to the Rastafari Coral Gardens Benevolent Society.
